summary.short: Illinois statute regulating private entities' possession, collection, use, disclosure and destruction of biometric identifiers and biometric information. Requires a public retention policy, written notice and release before collection, and bars sale or profit; gives aggrieved persons a private right of action with liquidated damages. Takes effect upon becoming law.
summary.long: The Act governs private entities (individuals, companies and other groups, excluding state and local government agencies and Illinois courts) that possess or collect biometric identifiers (retina or iris scans, fingerprints, voiceprints, hand or face geometry scans) and biometric information. Section 15 requires a publicly available written retention and destruction policy, with destruction when the initial purpose is satisfied or within 3 years of the last interaction, written notice and a written release before collection, and a bar on selling or profiting from such data and on most disclosures without consent or a legal exception. Storage must meet the industry's reasonable standard of care and be at least as protective as for other confidential information. Section 20 gives any aggrieved person a private right of action, with liquidated damages of $1,000 for negligent and $5,000 for intentional or reckless violations, or actual damages if greater, plus attorneys' fees and injunctive relief. Section 25 excludes financial institutions under Gramm-Leach-Bliley, matters governed by HIPAA and the X-Ray Retention Act, and government contractors working for government bodies. Section 30 is repealed; the Act takes effect upon becoming law (Section 99).

notes: Consolidated text with source notes; Sec. 30 is marked repealed internally (eff. 1-1-09) and no other instrument is repealed. Sec. 99 says the Act takes effect upon becoming law, while the source notes give eff. 10-3-08 for the original sections. The Act names no enforcement agency or designated authority; enforcement is by private right of action (Sec. 20). The regulated parties are the defined category 'private entity' (Sec. 10), not named firms. Sec. 25(c) excludes GLBA Title V financial institutions and Sec. 25(e) excludes contractors of State agencies or local governments working for them. Relations listed are non-conflict clauses, definitional references and source-note history, not amendments made by this text.

"Biometric identifier" means a retina or iris scan, fingerprint, voiceprint, or scan of hand or face geometry.
"Biometric information" means any information, regardless of how it is captured, converted, stored, or shared, based on an individual's biometric identifier used to identify an individual.
"Confidential and sensitive information" means personal information that can be used to uniquely identify an individual or an individual's account or property.
"Electronic signature" means an electronic sound, symbol, or process attached to or logically associated with a record and executed or adopted by a person with the intent to sign the record.
"Private entity" means any individual, partnership, corporation, limited liability company, association, or other group, however organized.
"Written release" means informed written consent, electronic signature, or, in the context of employment, a release executed by an employee as a condition of employment.

obligations.summary: A private entity in possession of biometric identifiers or biometric information must develop a written policy, made available to the public, establishing a retention schedule and guidelines for permanent destruction.

evidence.quote: must develop a written policy, made available to the public, establishing a retention schedule and guidelines for permanently destroying biometric identifiers and biometric information

obligations.summary: A private entity in possession of biometric identifiers or information must destroy them when the initial purpose is satisfied or within 3 years of the individual's last interaction, whichever occurs first, and must comply with its established retention schedule and destruction guidelines absent a valid warrant or subpoena.

evidence.quote: must comply with its established retention schedule and destruction guidelines

obligations.summary: Before collecting, capturing, purchasing, receiving or otherwise obtaining biometric identifiers or information, a private entity must inform the subject in writing that they are being collected or stored, and of the specific purpose and length of term.

evidence.quote: in writing that a biometric identifier or biometric information is being collected or stored

obligations.summary: Before obtaining a person's biometric identifier or information, a private entity must receive a written release executed by the subject or the subject's legally authorized representative.

obligations.summary: A private entity in possession of biometric identifiers or information may not disclose, redisclose, or otherwise disseminate them unless the subject consents, a financial transaction requires it, State or federal law or municipal ordinance requires it, or a valid warrant or subpoena requires it.
